title: Kid-Safe 'Freckle' Phone Builds Independence
paragraphs: Many parents want their children to become more independent, but they worry about giving them a smartphone with full access to the internet. A new phone for children called Freckle aims to solve this problem.

Freckle is a phone designed for children aged 7 to 13. It was developed by a company called Freckle together with a design studio called Body Shop. The phone uses a simple operating system called ClayOS. It does not have an internet browser, an app store, social media or video streaming apps such as YouTube.

Instead, the phone is designed to encourage children to go outside. It has a "Discovery Camera" that uses artificial intelligence to help children learn about plants and insects that they find. It also has "Quests," which are missions that send children to look for things such as bugs or flowers. Parents can create these missions, or they can use ones made by Freckle.

Children can only call and send messages to people their parents have approved. There is also a walkie-talkie feature for talking to other Freckle phones nearby. The phone also has a small map and can be used to pay for things like snacks or bus fares.
Parents can see where their child is on a map. They can also set "safe zones" and receive an alert when their child leaves them.

The phone has a small 3.1-inch screen and colorful buttons. It costs $199 to buy, and the phone service costs $25 a month after the first month. People in the US can order it now, and it is expected to start shipping in December 2026.
However, the phone has not been released yet, so experts have not been able to test how well it works. Some people have also asked how much parents should track their children.
